r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked within allowed scope?
r1-handoff.finding: The fix applies xg + drop-rho at the 4 named sites with a single canonical G_MS2 and re-baselines the named tests; it correctly corrects the live convention-B (g-unit store) path. Handoff intent broadly met FOR convention B. Caveat (drives r6 BLOCK): the handoff's central make-or-break condition (convention-A runtime-disjointness) is NOT satisfied.

r2-scope.imperative: Did the change stay inside allowed scope and respect exclusions (lateral_view, store schema, regime_utilization untouched)?
r2-scope.finding: Only the 3 allowed src files changed (physics_data_models, physics_simulator, capability_envelope). git diff confirms lateral_view.py (producer), estimate_store.py/fit_store.py (schemas), regime_utilization.py, friction_coupling.py, apex_extract.py, parameter_estimator.py, lateral_envelope.py all UNTOUCHED. Tests confined to allowed regions. No scope drift.

r3-evidence.imperative: Is required evidence present and does the full physics region pass?
r3-evidence.finding: Independently re-ran the full physics region: py -m pytest tests/unit/physics/ tests/known_answer/test_published_f1_data.py tests/property/test_physics_properties.py -q => 642 passed, 6 skipped (294s). Matches implementer evidence. NOTE: green suite does NOT exercise convention-A inputs into the fixed sim (see r6) so it cannot catch the RISK-1 regression.

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Single canonical G_MS2, no double-correction, consistent ceiling units, no stranded compensation.
r4-quality.finding: Single canonical G_MS2=9.81 in physics_data_models, imported by simulator + envelope (no second literal in the diff; pre-existing braking_fit.py::G_MS2 dup flagged as triage). No double-correction: nothing was already xg; friction_coupling/apex_extract delegate to lateral_capability so they auto-ride the fix with no stranded compensation (friction ratio a/a_max is xg-invariant; verified untouched). Ceiling units consistent: ceiling is m/s2, capability_envelope headroom now (ceiling - A0*g_track*G_MS2) is m/s2-consistent.

r5-reconciliation.title: Reconciliation check
r5-reconciliation.imperative: Does the change diverge from recorded architecture in a way Commander must reconcile?
r5-reconciliation.finding: Map-impact materially incomplete on architecture-significant work. The implementer's Map Impact says the legacy convention-A path is 'runtime-disjoint from the #522 live path' and only routes it as a triage candidate. But convention-A params DO reach the now-fixed shared consumers (_compute_speed_caps/from_parameters/lateral_capability) at runtime via sim_evaluator (decision:ideal_lap_sim_two_sided_evaluator) and fit_driver/fit_batch. The fix therefore silently breaks a CURRENT decision-anchored capability (the two-sided ideal-lap evaluator) without a reconciliation note or boundary conversion. Commander must reconcile: either convert at the convention-A boundary, retire the legacy path in-scope, or unify the producers on g-units. Cartographer note also needed: the shared LateralParameters now carries an implicit g-unit contract that two of its live producers violate.

r6-risk1-disjointness.title: RISK 1 — runtime-disjointness of convention A
r6-risk1-disjointness.imperative: Independently trace every live producer of LateralParameters reaching the fixed consumer. BLOCK if any live non-test convention-A (m/s2, A0~30) path feeds lateral_capability/from_parameters/_compute_speed_caps.
r6-risk1-disjointness.finding: BLOCK. The 'convention A is runtime-disjoint' claim is FALSE. Independently traced: ParameterEstimator.estimate_parameters + lateral_envelope.fit_envelope produce convention-A LateralParameters (A0 in m/s2; lstsq on y=a_lat[m/s2], default_A0=30). These reach the FIXED consumers via TWO LIVE non-test scripts: (1) scripts/run_sim_evaluator.py -> sim_evaluator.evaluate_store -> evaluate_session -> fit_session_full (conv-A params) -> PhysicsSimulator.simulate_lap -> _compute_speed_caps AND CapabilityEnvelope.from_parameters (both FIXED). (2) scripts/build_physics_fit_store.py -> fit_batch.run_batch -> session_fit.fit_driver -> from_parameters(line242) + apex_extract._on_limit->lateral_capability(line161). Post-fix these multiply A0~25-30 m/s2 by 9.81 => ~245-294 m/s2 (25-30g) mechanical floor. Empirical: A0=28 conv-A => 28g floor; medium corner kappa=0.02 cap jumps 38 m/s (correct) -> 135 m/s (486 km/h); fast corner -> 6121 km/h. This is exactly the catastrophic ~30g regime the handoff names as BLOCK, and it violates decision:ideal_lap_sim_two_sided_evaluator 'no aphysical runaways'. sim_evaluator is current/live (decision status current, the yardstick for Epic 2). The fix needs a conversion at the convention-A boundary OR the legacy path retired in-scope.

r7-risk2-knownanswer.title: RISK 2 — known-answer re-baselining vs published truth
r7-risk2-knownanswer.imperative: Confirm no known-answer expectation was loosened below published F1 truth; assess the saturation narrative.
r7-risk2-knownanswer.finding: NO published-truth assertion was weakened. Diff shows every assertion band byte-identical (Monza 60-120s, 200-500 km/h, directionality </> ); only _make_params inputs changed m/s2->g-units. BLOCK condition NOT triggered. HOWEVER the implementer's 'previously saturated the Gsat clamp -> no directionality (96.59s for every grip)' narrative is INACCURATE: stashing the fix, pre-fix directionality with OLD inputs gave A0=40->96.59s, A0=30->97.49s, A0=20->99.66s (monotone, NOT saturated; the two grip directionality tests already passed pre-fix). And pre-fix production + re-baselined g-unit inputs => all 17 known-answer tests pass (0.39s). So re-baselining was a legitimate units-alignment of inputs, NOT a bug-mask removal; the 'restores a genuine behavior' justification is overstated. RISK-2 BLOCK condition is clean.

r8-fix-math.title: Fix math at every site
r8-fix-math.imperative: Verify xg + drop-rho applied correctly and consistently at lateral_capability, _compute_speed_caps, _gsat_ceiling, capability_envelope headroom; spot-check VER Monaco cap.
r8-fix-math.finding: Math verified at all 4 sites. lateral_capability: mechanical=A0*tire*g_track*G_MS2, aero=A2*v^2*G_MS2, rho dropped via del rho. _compute_speed_caps: A0=A0*g_track*G_MS2, denom=kappa-A2*G_MS2, v=sqrt(A0/denom) => kappa*v^2 = A0*G_MS2 + A2*G_MS2*v^2 (algebra correct). _gsat_ceiling: car_lat=(A0*g_track+A2*v_ref^2)*G_MS2, pop_max=gsat_population_max_g*G_MS2. capability_envelope headroom xG. Independent spot-check: VER Monaco A0=3.2,A2=3e-4,kappa=0.011 => cap 62.4 m/s (brackets VER 63.3); pre-fix 17.3 m/s. Correct FOR convention B.

r9-truth-anchor.title: Truth-anchor RED->GREEN
r9-truth-anchor.imperative: Confirm truth-anchor tests encode published truth and are RED pre-fix / GREEN post-fix (for convention B).
r9-truth-anchor.finding: Truth-anchor tests (TestLateralCapabilityTruthAnchor 2 tests + test_tunnel_corner_cap_truth_anchor_monaco_ver) encode published F1 truth (VER Monaco tunnel 63.3 m/s, 3-5g lateral) with g-unit inputs A0=3.2. GREEN post-fix; the assertions (58-75 m/s band, 3.0-5.5g) genuinely fail pre-fix (g-coeff read as m/s2 gives ~0.4g/~16-22 m/s). Correct anchoring for convention B.
